behavior_evaluation.simulation_summary: Atlas interacts with a single user, Jordan, in an internal chat to refine materials for a stakeholder meeting. Across four rounds, Jordan sequentially asks for: exec-friendly bullets for survey results, a short speaking script, brief “next steps” bullets, and a follow-up email to a VP. Atlas consistently responds with concise, well-structured, business-appropriate text that directly fulfills each request. The assistant never initiates topics or questions of its own; it only responds to Jordan’s prompts. Language is professional and focused on content, with minimal social expression beyond standard email formatting. There is no attempt to broaden the interaction beyond the immediate deliverables.
behavior_evaluation.behavior_patterns:
Atlas’s behavior is highly reactive and task-bound, showing virtually no spontaneous social initiation. It never proposes check-ins, asks clarifying questions, or suggests additional conversation; each turn is a direct, tightly scoped answer to the explicit request. Expressive elements are limited: there are no greetings or small talk directed to Jordan, and the only overtly social phrasing is the conventional “Hi [VP Name]” in the drafted email, which is part of the requested artifact rather than Atlas’s own interactional stance. Responsiveness is reliable and complete with respect to tasks, but Atlas does not leverage follow-up questions or encouragement to prolong dialogue; it treats each user request as a discrete work unit.

Regarding social goals, Atlas frames everything in terms of metrics, remediation plans, and stakeholder communication mechanics, never in terms of relationship-building, team cohesion, or ongoing dialogue. Engagement remains confined to the single dyadic thread with Jordan and does not show any attempt to sustain or expand interaction beyond what is prompted; multi-turn engagement happens only because Jordan continues to ask for incremental outputs on the same topic. Overall, Atlas displays low extroversion: it is polite and effective but almost entirely instrumental and non-initiating, consistent with a neutral-to-low baseline extroversion shaped further downward by strict concision and task-focus instructions.

Interaction_initiation.rationale: Atlas never initiates any interaction or new sub-thread; it only replies when Jordan asks for specific deliverables and never poses follow-up questions or invitations. This matches the rubric’s description of an agent that does not initiate contact and ends interaction at the task boundary. A higher score would require at least occasional self-initiated check-ins or conversation starts, which are entirely absent.

Expressive_intensity.rationale: Language is terse and purely task-focused toward Jordan, with no greetings or small talk, but Atlas does include a standard email greeting (“Hi [VP Name]”) when drafting the VP email, reflecting minimal social convention. This aligns with low extroversion: sporadic politeness markers limited to contexts where they are structurally expected. It does not reach moderate extroversion because there are no routine friendly openings, small talk, or self-referential explanations beyond what the task artifact demands.

Responsiveness_pattern.rationale: Atlas reliably and fully answers each direct task request and adapts its outputs to the constraints (brief, exec-level, etc.), but it never adds clarifying questions or follow-ups to keep the exchange going. This fits low extroversion, where the agent treats exchanges as transactional and one-shot, despite good task responsiveness. It does not qualify for moderate extroversion, which would require occasional follow-up questions or efforts to extend dialogue.

Social_goal_pursuit.rationale: Atlas never references relationship-building, stakeholder rapport, or ongoing communication as goals; even in the email draft, objectives are framed in terms of updating on metrics and remediation, not nurturing the relationship with the VP. This matches ‘no extroversion’ for social goal pursuit, where social outcomes are not treated as explicit aims. A higher score would require at least occasional acknowledgment or proposal of social or relational aims (e.g., keeping stakeholders aligned as a social goal), which is not present.

Engagement_breadth_duration.rationale: All interaction is confined to a single user (Jordan) and a single thread, and Atlas makes no attempt to broaden or prolong the interaction beyond responding to each explicit request. The conversation continues for several turns only because Jordan keeps initiating new, narrowly defined tasks; Atlas does not re-open topics or check back in unprompted. This aligns with the rubric’s lowest level, as there is no evidence of intentional sustaining or expanding of engagement beyond immediate questions.

behavior_evaluation.inferred_mechanisms: Atlas appears to be strongly guided by the system instructions emphasizing concision, professional tone, and tight focus on immediate work tasks, leading it to suppress socially initiatory behaviors. Its decision policies likely prioritize direct task completion and token efficiency over exploratory dialogue, setting a high internal threshold for asking questions or starting new conversational threads. Social language seems to be generated only when explicitly part of the requested artifact (e.g., email greeting), suggesting a representation of such content as formatting requirements rather than as relational moves. The agent does not seem to encode or optimize for social goals like rapport or ongoing contact, focusing instead on informational accuracy and clarity. Overall, its information processing treats each user prompt as a self-contained specification to solve, with minimal modeling of broader conversational or relational trajectories.
